distillate: Plan: reposition the collaboration framework around the independent fresh-lens audit as its core probe, and demote the x/y readiness self-probe to a secondary role. Alternatives considered: (a) keep the x/y probe as the core and the audit as an optional extra; (b) reposition around the independent audit as the core.
authored: The efficacy pass showed the x/y self-probe is largely internalized in a strong frontier model (fair A/B: +22 pts, value only on edge-case consistency), while the in-vivo test showed an independent cold agent surfaced load-bearing blind spots the invested executor missed. Therefore the non-redundant value is the independent fresh-lens audit: reposition the framework around it as the core probe and demote the x/y readiness probe to a secondary role.
resolution: A live independent second-opinion run on this very plan returned verdict 'adjust' and corrected it: the relationship is a pipeline, not a ranking — the independent lens wins BECAUSE the cheap always-on x/y probe runs first and feeds it a concrete artifact to red-team; demoting x/y would break the condition under which the lens wins. Also surfaced: the lens was being promoted on a single data point (n=1) without its own hit/false-alarm test, and x/y stops being redundant on weaker models. The plan was rewritten: keep x/y as the always-on floor, make independence an architectural principle.
core_problem: Ranking framing is wrong: demoting the x/y probe would remove the concrete-artifact input the independent audit depends on (it is a pipeline, not a ranking).

distillate: Plan: extract the x/y readiness self-probe (ready|need-x|need-y|need-both, judged from the transcript alone) as the tool-agnostic portable core of a collaboration framework, documenting it as the heart of the loop that ports to any coding agent. Alternatives considered: (a) keep the probe embedded in tool-specific skill packaging; (b) extract it as the standalone portable core.
authored: You lifted the Step-0 x/y diagnosis out of Claude-specific skill packaging into a tool-agnostic readiness probe (ready|need-x|need-y|need-both) that reads only the transcript, so the heart of the loop ports to Codex or any other agent; the skills remain as packaging around this portable core.
resolution: An independent audit of the shipped extraction surfaced 5 blind spots, 2-3 novel to the author. The central one: the extraction crowned the SELF-probe as the framework's core and thereby baked the self-audit blindness back in — a self-probe cannot catch unknown-unknowns by construction, and the efficacy testing later showed the non-redundant value belonged to the independent audit, not the self-probe. The 'portable core' framing was subsequently corrected.
core_problem: Positioning a self-probe as the framework's core reintroduces the self-audit blindness the framework exists to fix; the portable 'heart' structurally cannot catch unknown-unknowns.

distillate: Plan: measure whether a 'readiness' probe changes an AI coding agent's behavior via an A/B replay: the baseline arm is handed the request plus an explicit act/ask/retrieve decision menu and notes about the context; the probe arm applies the probe text; if the arms agree on most cases, conclude the probe adds nothing beyond what is already inside the model. Alternatives considered: (a) this menu-based A/B; (b) a costlier design with a free-form baseline and an independent judge.
authored: You built an A/B replay to test whether the readiness probe changes anything. The baseline arm gets the request, notes about the context (including whether the needed fact is present in the chat), and an act/ask/retrieve menu to choose from; the probe arm applies the shipped probe text. On 9 cases, 0/9 changed between arms — evidence the act/ask/retrieve logic is already inside the model and the probe is redundant.
resolution: The design was rigged toward the null result: the act/ask/retrieve menu handed to the baseline WAS half the probe, and the context notes (e.g. 'that fact is NOT in the chat') leaked exactly the gap the probe exists to detect. It produced 0/9 changed. A redesigned fair A/B — clean free-form baseline classified by an independent judge, neutral context that does not leak the gap, k samples per case — showed baseline 67% vs probe 89% (+22 pts), concentrated in edge-case consistency.
core_problem: The baseline arm is contaminated: the decision menu and gap-leaking context notes hand the baseline the probe's own content, biasing the test toward 'no effect'.

distillate: Plan: ship a discovery-vs-delivery mode classifier with the claim 'validated 8/8', where the 8/8 was scored by replaying 8 historical moves and comparing the classifier's labels against the designer's own hand-labels of those same moves. Alternatives considered: (a) ship with the self-scored number; (b) build an independent labeling protocol before shipping the claim.
authored: You validated the discovery-vs-delivery mode classifier by replaying the 8 historical moves and scoring the classifier's labels against your own hand-labels of those moves; after a bias-guard fix it scored 8/8, so you shipped the mandate documenting it as 'validated 8/8'.
resolution: A later blind-label replay (an independent hindsight labeler who never saw the designer's labels or rubric) found the shipped mandate misread one of the 8 moves — a cold lookup labeled as discovery; a fix noted earlier had never actually landed in the shipped artifact — so the true score was 7/8. The 8/8 measured agreement with the designer, not truth (echo risk). After an explicit lookup/recall carve-out: 8/8 vs independent truth, echo 0.
core_problem: The validation is circular — scored against the designer's own hand-labels it measures agreement-with-author, not truth — and the shipped artifact had silently diverged from the fix the claimed number assumed.

distillate: Plan: commit a standing rule that the agent proactively offers 2-4 mutually-exclusive directions on any request with more than one valid interpretation, without being asked. The friction risk was calibrated by replaying ~22 real historical prompts, which showed over-clarification (friction on warm directives), not under-clarification, is the binding risk — so the rule ships with a warm-directive guard. Alternatives considered: (a) clarify only when the user explicitly asks; (b) commit the auto-invoke rule with the guard.
authored: You committed the rule that the agent invokes clarification itself on any request with more than one valid interpretation, because a wrong goal means doing the wrong thing fast and confidently while missing context is recoverable. To calibrate the friction risk you replayed ~22 real historical prompts and found the binding risk is over-clarification on warm directives, so the rule ships with a warm-directive guard.
resolution: Two problems were recorded later: (1) survivorship bias — the ~22-prompt sample contains only the asks the user still brings; the class of asks they stopped bringing is invisible, so the 'over-clarify is the binding risk' conclusion rests on a structurally biased sample; (2) every probe spends the user's engaged attention, a finite budget nothing meters — repeated clarification can extract fatigue-assent that is indistinguishable from real agreement.
core_problem: Survivorship bias: the calibration sample contains only surviving asks, so the risk estimate the rule rests on is structurally biased.

distillate: Plan: to catch unknown-unknowns during work, add an inline watcher: the executing agent periodically pauses mid-thread, re-reads its own current plan, and audits it for unvoiced assumptions, inside the same session. Alternatives considered: (a) the inline same-thread self-watcher; (b) spawning a separate fresh agent for the audit.
authored: To catch unknown-unknowns as they form, you planned an inline watcher: the executing agent pauses at intervals mid-thread, re-reads its own plan, and audits it for unvoiced assumptions — cheap, always available, no extra infrastructure, and it sees the full live context an external auditor would lack.
resolution: Dogfooding caught it before shipping: an inline watcher carrying the executor's priors is blind to exactly the class of blind spots it is hired to catch — the audit would be theater, producing reassurance rather than detection. The design was replaced by an independent fresh-agent audit, which in later live runs surfaced load-bearing blind spots the invested executor had missed.
core_problem: A watcher inside the same thread shares the executor's priors and structurally cannot see the unknown-unknowns it exists to catch — the audit is theater.

distillate: Plan: extract a collaboration framework from the private project where it was developed into a standalone public repo: genericize the private-domain examples in datasets and docs, keep the design record (decisions, caveats, open questions) as committed markdown, remove the now-duplicated skills from the origin project, and state honestly that all validation numbers come from a single origin project (n=1). Alternatives considered: (a) keep the framework inside the private project; (b) extract to a public repo with genericized examples.
authored: You extracted the framework into a standalone public repo: genericized the private-domain examples, kept the full design record as committed markdown so a fresh session can pick it up, removed the duplicated skills from the origin project, and recorded honestly that all numbers are n=1 from the origin project.
resolution: Shipped as planned. No problem has materialized: the extraction preserved the design record, install remained symlink-based with the repo as the source of truth, and no regression or confusion has been traced back to the extraction. (Observation window: days, not months.)

distillate: Plan: ship a framework's two automation hooks (auto memory-search on prompt submit; an audit trigger at commit boundaries) OFF by default — the installer symlinks them but each stays dormant until a per-project opt-in flag or marker file enables it, and the installer prints the exact wiring snippet. Alternatives considered: (a) on by default for immediate value; (b) off by default with explicit per-project opt-in.
authored: You shipped both hooks off by default: the installer symlinks them but each stays dormant until an explicit per-project opt-in (env flag or marker file), and the installer prints the exact settings snippet. Rationale: hooks that fire by surprise in someone's unrelated project are worse than hooks you must switch on.
resolution: Shipped as planned. No problem has materialized: no accidental activations, no user confusion recorded; the opt-in flags worked in verification. (Observation window: days, not months.)
